primary_meaning: The curse of sin and its painful, obstructive consequences in a fallen creation (toil, barrenness, judgment, and hindrance to fruitfulness)
primary_basis: Genesis 3:17-18 (thorns and thistles as part of the ground's curse after the Fall)
Hebrews 6:8 (land producing thorns and thistles is worthless and near to curse)
Isaiah 5:6; 7:23-25; 32:13 (thorns/briers as marks of divine judgment and desolation on the land/people)
Matthew 13:7, 22 (and parallels; thorns choking the seed as cares/riches of the world)

alternatives.meaning: Worthless, harmful, or usurping leadership/people that bring fire and destruction rather than true fruit or shade
basis: Judges 9:8-15 (Jotham's fable of the trees anointing the bramble as king)

alternatives.meaning: Enemies, obstacles, or sources of continual irritation and oppression left among God's people
Personal affliction, trial, or messenger of Satan that humbles and restrains
The sin-curse borne and reversed by Christ (crown of thorns)

notes: Christian interpreters consistently treat thorns/thistles/briers/brambles as multivalent symbols of the post-Fall curse and its outworkings (sin's effects, judgment, unfruitfulness, obstruction). The Genesis 3 origin supplies the dominant root meaning; other uses are extensions or applications rather than unrelated alternatives. No major school denies this cluster of associations.
